name: Shallum
overview: Shallum was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim known primarily as the father of Jehikhiah, who played a role in assisting the defeated people of Judah. His identity is rooted in this specific familial and tribal connection without additional personal details recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Shallum means 'peace, well-being, prosperity,' reflecting a positive Hebrew meaning. It is a proper name mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:12 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Shallum is noted as the father of Jehikhiah, who aided the defeated Judaites, establishing a direct paternal relationship. He is also explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim. No other family relationships are recorded beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Shallum's significance in Scripture comes through his son Jehikhiah, whose actions to support the defeated inhabitants of Judah are recorded, highlighting Shallum's familial link to a moment of compassion and assistance in Israel's history. His mention in 2 Chronicles 28:12 situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal and social dynamics during a time of conflict.
